source.work: Auth.js (NextAuth v5) documentation, middleware and the authorized callback
source.paraphrase: Middleware protects a route only when the authorized callback returns a decision based on the request. Returning true always admits every request.

invariants.why: An authorized callback that always returns true keeps the middleware file while protecting nothing behind it.
invariants.fixHint: Decide on the session: return !!auth?.user, or check a role on the request path that needs it.
invariants.avoid: A block body ending in return true is the same unconditional yes as the arrow form.

source.work: Auth.js (NextAuth v5) documentation, server-side session access
source.locator: auth() versus next-auth/react in server code
source.paraphrase: Server code reads the session with auth(). The next-auth/react helpers are client bindings; importing them into routes and server components pulls the wrong layer.

invariants.why: In the selected server-owned paths, session access must use the project's server auth API. A valid leading use client directive exempts a client module; importing client components for rendering is a separate project boundary decision.
invariants.fixHint: Import { auth } from the server auth module and call await auth() in routes and server components.
invariants.avoid: This is an optional module-boundary policy, not proof that every next-auth/react import is invalid. Only literal import/export sources and first literal require/import arguments are checked. Client directives must be in the top-level directive prologue; nested strings and late directives do not exempt the module. Cross-file client subtrees and symbol usage require project evidence.

source.paraphrase: The jwt callback runs on every request, but user and account arrive only on sign-in. A callback that spreads them unconditionally reads fields that are absent on later calls.

invariants.why: Spreading sign-in-only fields without a guard crashes or mints malformed tokens on every subsequent request.
invariants.fixHint: Guard the callback: handle !token first, or apply user and account fields only inside if (user).
invariants.avoid: Passing the token through untouched is still unguarded when later code assumes the sign-in fields exist.

source.locator: what the session callback returns to the client
source.paraphrase: The session callback shapes the object the client receives. Long-lived refresh credentials must stay server-side; only short-lived access data goes out.

invariants.why: A refresh token sent to the client lets anyone holding it mint fresh sessions until it is revoked.
invariants.fixHint: Keep refresh credentials in the JWT or the database. Return only the access data the UI needs.
invariants.avoid: Aliasing the refresh value under another key still sends it to the client.

source.paraphrase: The redirect callback runs whenever the user is sent to a callback URL. By default only URLs on the same host as the origin are allowed; the documented example allows relative paths and same-origin URLs and otherwise returns baseUrl.

invariants.why: Returning url unchanged removes the same-host check, so a crafted callbackUrl sends users from your login page to any site.
invariants.fixHint: Return url only when it starts with / or its origin equals baseUrl; otherwise return baseUrl.
invariants.avoid: Flags a redirect callback inside callbacks whose whole body is url or x.url (concise arrow, or a block with that single return; comments are ignored). Any extra statement, such as an origin check, passes. Warn only: the matcher cannot see an allowlist enforced elsewhere.

source.paraphrase: The jwt callback controls what is encoded into the session token stored in the client cookie; only minimal identity claims needed for authorization should be added.

invariants.why: Copying password hashes, private keys, or secrets onto token bloat cookie size and expose credentials if the token secret leaks or is decoded.
invariants.fixHint: Assign only safe identifiers such as token.sub = user.id or token.role = user.role inside the jwt callback.
invariants.avoid: Only direct assignments to token.<sensitiveField> or returned object keys inside a jwt callback are matched.
